source: Arosa planning assumption for a New York City mid-rise residential building, ordered by the UniFormat elements (substructure, shell, interiors, services, sitework) that RSMeans Square Foot Costs uses for its 4 to 7 storey apartment model; shares are rounded planning figures, not a published cost index or a contractor estimate

hard.label: Site work and demolition
hard.note: Demolition of what stands, excavation support, utilities to the lot line and sidewalks

hard.label: Foundations and substructure
hard.note: Footings or mat, cellar walls, slab on grade and waterproofing

hard.label: Structure
hard.note: Frame, floor and roof slabs, stairs

hard.label: Facade and roofing
hard.note: Exterior walls, windows, roofing and terraces

hard.label: Interiors and finishes
hard.note: Partitions, doors, kitchens, baths, flooring and finishes

hard.label: Vertical transportation
hard.note: Passenger elevator; a walk-up building has none and its share goes to the other lines

hard.label: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing
hard.note: Heating and cooling, plumbing, fire protection, electrical and low voltage

hard.label: General conditions and GC fee
hard.note: Site staff, temporary works, insurance carried by the contractor and the contractor's fee

soft.label: Architecture and engineering
soft.note: Architect, structural, MEP and civil engineers, expediting and surveys

soft.label: Permits and filing fees
soft.note: Buildings, utility and other agency fees

soft.label: Legal and closing
soft.note: Development and financing legal work, title and loan closing

soft.label: Insurance
soft.note: Builder's risk, general liability and owner policies during construction

soft.label: Developer fee
soft.note: The developer's fee for running the project
